summary: TCS builds, changes and runs computer systems and related business work for organisations such as banks, shops and manufacturers.
description: Many large organisations need outside specialists to make their computer systems work. For an illustrative example, a bank might pay a technology company to improve its account software and keep it running. TCS takes on agreed projects or continuing services of this kind. It supplies people, technical work and relevant software; it does not own the client’s banking business.
money: The organisation buying the work pays TCS under a contract. Payment may cover an agreed project, staff time or an ongoing service, depending on the terms. TCS pays employees, outside specialists, software and equipment costs and the costs of managing the work. Fees received are not all profit.
customers: Businesses and public organisations that need technology or related work done: banks, retailers, manufacturers and others. A customer’s sector describes who buys the service, not an industry that TCS owns.
drivers: Customers willing to spend, work actually started and completed, agreed prices, employee costs, how efficiently teams work and whether customers pay on time.

groups.title: Build or improve computer systems
groups.examples: Application development, consulting, business software and cloud work.
groups.explanation: An application is a computer program used for a task. TCS can help design, build, test or change it. Cloud work can involve moving programs or data to computing services accessed over a network, and making that change work properly.

groups.title: Keep systems and business work running
groups.examples: Managed technology services, cybersecurity and business-process services.
groups.explanation: Managed services means taking responsibility for agreed ongoing work. That can include maintaining systems, helping protect information or carrying out defined business tasks. For an illustration of outsourced business work, a customer might pay for processing invoices; the actual duties depend on the contract. The customer pays for reliable work, not simply the presence of a team.

groups.title: Use data, AI and engineering skills
groups.examples: Data analysis, artificial-intelligence and engineering-related work.
groups.explanation: A customer may want help finding patterns in information or improving a process. TCS must do the paid work promised and make it usable. Naming an AI project does not prove that it has earned revenue or saved money.

groups.title: Reusable software offerings
groups.examples: TCS BaNCS, TCS iON and other products or platforms.
groups.explanation: A platform is a reusable software base that can be set up for different customers. The contract determines payment for its use, setup or support. A product name does not tell us its separately reported profit.

basics.title: The same customer can buy several services
basics.text: A bank could buy software development, security and continuing support. The financial report’s banking-customer category can include all those jobs. Do not add a service category to a customer-industry category as though they were separate sales.

steps.title: Agree the problem and the paid job
steps.text: The customer and TCS agree what must change or keep working, who does what, the price and how completion will be checked.

steps.title: Assign people and carry out the work
steps.text: Teams build and test software, move systems or run the agreed service. TCS pays the people and tools needed while doing the job.

steps.title: Record earned work and send bills
steps.text: The accounting rules and contract determine when work counts as revenue. The date a bill is sent can differ from the date work is recorded.

steps.title: Collect payment and meet continuing promises
steps.text: The customer pays under agreed terms. TCS must still correct covered problems, meet service promises and compete to keep or expand the relationship.

specifics.title: A large contract is future work, not cash already received
specifics.text: Total contract value is the announced value over the contract’s stated life. The work may take years. Changes, cancellations and the pace at which work starts affect what becomes current sales and payment.

specifics.title: Employees can be paid while waiting for work
specifics.text: Utilisation measures how much available staff time is used on customer work under the company’s definition. Wages continue when people are training or between assignments. Lower staff cost alone is not useful if quality or the skills needed suffer.

specifics.title: Faster work can help the customer without increasing TCS profit
specifics.text: AI or other tools may reduce the time a job needs. TCS may benefit from lower costs, but the customer may ask for a lower price. Read who keeps the saving and whether it brings new paid work.

watch: Are signed contracts turning into work and bills?
A deal can cover several future years.
Compare contract announcements with sales and comments on when teams start. Check whether a deal is new work or a renewal of something TCS already does.
Keeping an essential system running differs from funding an optional improvement.
Read spending decisions by customer industry and country. Look for work that has actually started rather than assuming broad interest in technology means approved budgets.
Are teams covering their costs while meeting promises?
Employee pay, prices and efficient work affect what remains from fees.
Read wages, people leaving, outside-specialist costs and the share of staff time on customer work. Ask whether claimed savings show up in actual earnings without harming service.
Are customers paying for recorded work?
Work recorded or billed is not always cash received.
Read unpaid customer bills and unbilled revenue: work recorded as earned but not yet invoiced. Compare those balances with sales, billing schedules and cash from normal operations.
Is AI work paid and useful to the customer?
A named offering or training count is not an earned fee.
Look for work put into use, contract scope and how the company defines AI-related sales. Check whether it is genuinely additional work or a label on existing services.
risks: New projects can wait while customers reconsider budgets.
Software faults, missed service promises or exposed data can cause penalties, repeated work and lost trust.
People cost more than contracts earn
Wages, scarce skills or customer pressure for lower prices can reduce profit.
Automation, exchange rates, data rules and restrictions on where employees can work can change demand and costs.
context: An old customer still has to choose to stay

Knowing a customer’s systems can help TCS do useful work, but contracts still face price and quality checks and competition. A long relationship does not guarantee that future projects or renewals will be won.
quiz: Can the whole announced value of a long contract be counted as this year’s sales?
No. Sales depend on the work earned under the accounting rules over the contract’s life. Bills and customer payments can happen at different times too.
sources: Official services, products and industry directory

financialNotes.title: Read margins as published
financialNotes.text: The existing table contains customer-industry revenue and reported margin percentages. It deliberately does not multiply rounded percentages by revenue to manufacture profit amounts. A higher margin percentage does not establish the largest total profit contribution.

financialNotes.title: Do not turn a service brand into a segment
financialNotes.text: Cloud, AI and BaNCS can serve several client industries. The table is not a profit report for each platform, nor a replacement for the consolidated profit and cash-flow reconciliation.
